title: The Erdős-Gallai bound for consecutive even cycle lengths
summary: Erdős and Gallai in 1959 proved the seminal result that every $n$-vertex graph with no cycle of length at least $2t+2$ has at most $\tfrac{2t+1}{2}(n-1)$ edges. We prove the extension that, for every sufficiently large $t$, the same quantity is also the sharp extremal bound for graphs with no $t$ consecutive even cycle lengths, resolving a conjecture of Verstraëte. Thus, at the Erdős-Gallai threshold, forcing an entire interval of even cycle lengths costs no more than forcing its longest member.
